rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify poorly resolved pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The midrange temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Make the gradient slightly shallower to test whether the sole under-resolved pair responds to slope, while keeping the last peak likely below 10 minutes. Holding the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed makes this comparison diagnostic.

The critical pair improves with a shallower gradient, so reduce the slope further while raising the starting organic fraction to remove low-organic waiting time. This should improve resolution while targeting last-peak elution within 10 minutes; the first peak’s estimated elution fraction near 0.13–0.14 makes early retention worth monitoring.

Injection 3 already achieved the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark while testing a shorter separation. Shifting the starting fraction upward while preserving the 0.05-per-minute gradient slope should advance elution with limited selectivity changes, though early-peak and critical-pair resolution need checking.
Keep injection 4’s gradient fixed and test whether a 5 °C temperature increase improves the critical pair’s selectivity while shortening retention. Injection 3 remains the maximum-score fallback.

The critical pair nearly co-elutes at 45 °C, so test higher temperature for renewed separation beyond a possible elution-order crossover. Restore injection 3’s lower starting organic fraction to provide more resolution margin for other pairs while temperature shortens the separation.

Lower the starting organic fraction to test whether the newly limiting early-middle pair gains resolution at 55 °C. The slightly steeper gradient may help preserve separation of the later close pair, with sufficient time margin to keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Shorten injection 7’s gradient to seek a faster maximum-score separation. The steeper slope may improve the temperature-reordered close pair, while the other moderately resolved pair has some margin at R = 2.23.

Test a shorter gradient while lowering the starting organic fraction to protect the early-middle pair, whose resolution decreased when the gradient was shortened. The later close pair improved slightly with the steeper slope, making this a promising route to a faster fully resolved separation.

Injection 9 is the fastest fully resolved method so far; now test a substantially cooler selectivity regime with a shorter gradient. Cooling may separate the critical cluster differently, while the higher starting organic fraction and steeper gradient offset increased retention.

Test a faster high-temperature regime for separation beyond another possible selectivity crossover in the early-middle cluster. The lower-temperature trial created several overlaps; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Shorten the gradient at 60 °C to test whether the remaining close pair separates further after its apparent elution-order crossover. The other pairs have resolution margin, and this directly measures slope sensitivity in the promising fast regime.

Raise the starting organic fraction to test whether it improves the remaining crossover pair more effectively than slope alone. The longer, slightly shallower gradient should protect the neighboring pair, but resolution of the earliest two peaks will need checking.

Test intermediate low-temperature selectivity with a gradient shorter than injection 3’s fully resolved method. This may avoid both the overlaps seen at 25 °C and the critical-pair crossover near 45 °C, while targeting elution before 8 minutes.

Shorten the fastest confirmed maximum-score method by two gradient minutes to establish its speed limit. Both limiting pairs were only just above R = 1.5 in injection 9, so this is a boundary test rather than an assumed improvement.

Trim injection 9’s gradient endpoint to 0.65 while preserving its successful 0.075-per-minute slope. Its last peak eluted near organic fraction 0.57, so all peaks should retain their separation while the programmed gradient finishes four minutes earlier.

Test a steep gradient at 60 °C to seek separation beyond the early-middle pair’s crossover, using the lowest starting organic fraction to protect neighboring peaks. This explores a substantially faster regime while retaining injection 16 as a confirmed maximum-score method.

Fine-tune the successful 55 °C regime with a slope between injections 8 and 9 and a higher starting fraction than injection 9. This targets slightly faster last-peak elution while keeping both limiting pairs above R = 1.5.

Reduce injection 18’s slope slightly from 0.0667 to 0.065 organic fraction per minute to bring its R = 1.47 pair above threshold. This should retain the later pair’s resolution and give a fully resolved separation near 7.8 minutes.

Test a slightly shallower slope than injection 19 to increase the limiting pair’s resolution margin while preserving full resolution of the later close pair. Since the maximum CRF is already achieved, this run targets a more robust maximum-score method rather than a higher score.

Slightly flatten injection 6’s gradient to improve its R = 1.41 pair while retaining the later pair’s R = 1.74 margin. This targets a maximum-score method with greater minimum-resolution margin, with last-peak elution expected below 10 minutes.

Reduce the slope slightly from injection 21 to improve its limiting R = 1.57 pair while aiming to preserve the later pair’s margin. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially yielding a maximum-score method with better minimum resolution.

Test a slope of 0.08 organic fraction per minute, between the fully resolved injection 9 and the faster but under-resolved injection 15. This probes the speed boundary more closely while retaining the confirmed maximum-score methods as fallbacks.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 22 to test whether both limiting pairs retain approximately R = 1.7 while the last peak stays below 10 minutes. The maximum CRF is already secured; this targets additional resolution margin rather than a higher score.

Trim the gradient window while keeping the slope close to injection 22, which achieved CRF 1.000 with minimum resolution 1.70. The last peak’s estimated elution fraction is about 0.54, so ending at 0.60 should preserve full elution below 10 minutes without the unused high-organic ramp.
